findings.title: Check the shared deadline before returning a direct posterior
findings.body: `direct()` constructs a Budget but never calls `budget.check()`. Budget construction validates only that the start time is in the past, so a call with `processing_begin=time.monotonic()-11` still returns a posterior, and `.mean()` can return a prediction without any deadline check. This bypasses the declared 10-second failure rule for D, whereas `marked()` rejects the same expired start immediately. Check the budget at entry and before returning the posterior.

overall_explanation: The Gaussian completion, shared-noise normalization, and differentiable conditional likelihood appear consistent on inspection. However, the direct operator fails to enforce its shared processing deadline. Review was limited to the supplied source bundle; no tests were executed.
